context: Synthetic ADAS labeling-service demo. Submitted annotations needed one explicit, immutable validation boundary so ambiguous coordinates, provenance and ontology metadata do not enter later labeling workflows.
decision: Implement a Python standard-library validator for schema 1.0 annotations using integer half-open pixel-edge coordinates. Accept right and bottom endpoints equal to frame width and height, including the complete frame and lower-right one-pixel box. Reject invalid inputs with deterministic code-and-field errors carried by AnnotationValidationError without mutating input.
rationale: ADR-0001 and ADAS-LBL-001 revision 3 define half-open pixel edges and make W/H valid endpoints. ADAS-LBL-002 revision 2 requires input provenance, while revision history and dataset release remain deferred. ADAS-LBL-003 revision 1 fixes the ontology and allowed classes. A pure standard-library function keeps this feature limited to validation and makes boundary behavior directly testable.
alternatives: Inclusive pixel indices were not selected because they conflict with ADR-0001 and create off-by-one adapter risk.
Normalized or fractional coordinates were not selected because the approved contract requires integer pixel edges and forbids silent rounding or conversion.
Third-party validation packages and web frameworks were not selected because the feature requires no dependency, transport or persistence layer.

candidate_lesson: Adapter-facing annotation contracts should state half-open edge semantics explicitly and test both the complete-frame box and the lower-right one-pixel box so valid W/H endpoints are not rejected.
